hints: Differentiate displacement $s(t) = 0.3t^2 + 0.6t$ with respect to $t$ to find the velocity expression.
Substitute $t = 4$ into $v(t)$ to find the velocity.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the velocity at $t = 4\text{ s}$:
$$v(4) = 0.6(4) + 0.6 = 2.4 + 0.6 = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Differentiate the displacement function to find the velocity expression for $0 \le t \le 4$:
$$s(t) = 0.3t^2 + 0.6t$$
$$v(t) = \frac{ds}{dt} = 2(0.3)t + 0.6 = 0.6t + 0.6$$

ai_rubric.Differentiating Motion Functions: Differentiates to get $v = 0.6t + 0.6$ and evaluates $v(4) = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Integrate acceleration $a(t) = 0.3 t^{1/2}$ for $t \ge 4$: $v(t) = \frac{0.3 t^{3/2}}{1.5} + c = 0.2 t^{3/2} + c$.
Use the boundary condition from part (a): $v(4) = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find the constant $c = 1.4$.
walkthrough:
Integrate acceleration $a(t) = 0.3 t^{1/2}$ to find velocity for $t \ge 4$:
$$v(t) = \int 0.3 t^{1/2}\,dt = \frac{0.3 t^{3/2}}{\frac{3}{2}} + c = 0.2 t^{3/2} + c$$

Use continuity of velocity at $t = 4\text{ s}$ ($v(4) = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$):
$$3 = 0.2(4^{3/2}) + c = 0.2(8) + c = 1.6 + c \implies c = 3 - 1.6 = 1.4$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Integrate acceleration to obtain the velocity function for $t \ge 4$:
$$a(t) = 0.3t^{1/2}$$
$$v(t) = \int 0.3t^{1/2}\,dt = 0.3 \times \frac{t^{3/2}}{\frac{3}{2}} + c = 0.2t^{3/2} + c$$

Step 2: Determine the integration constant $c$:
Because there is no sudden change in velocity at $t = 4$, $v(4) = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$3 = 0.2(4^{3/2}) + c$$
Since $4^{3/2} = (\sqrt{4})^3 = 2^3 = 8$:
$$3 = 0.2(8) + c = 1.6 + c$$
$$c = 3 - 1.6 = 1.4$$
Thus, for $t \ge 4$, the velocity function is:
$$v(t) = 0.2t^{3/2} + 1.4$$

ai_rubric.Integrating Motion Functions: Integrates $a$ to get $v = 0.2t^{3/2} + c$, uses $v(4) = 3$ to find $c = 1.4$, and solves $0.2T^{3/2} + 1.4 = 14.2$ to obtain $T = 16$.

hints: Find the distance in the first stage ($0 \le t \le 4$): $s(4) = 0.3(4^2) + 0.6(4) = 7.2\text{ m}$.
Evaluate the definite integral ($96.16\text{ m}$) and add $7.2\text{ m}$ to get the total distance.
walkthrough:
Calculate the distance travelled during the first 4 seconds ($0 \le t \le 4$):
$$s_1 = s(4) = 0.3(4^2) + 0.6(4) = 0.3(16) + 2.4 = 4.8 + 2.4 = 7.2\text{ m}$$

Integrate velocity to find the distance travelled from $t = 4$ to $t = 16$:
$$s_2 = \int_4^{16} (0.2t^{3/2} + 1.4)\,dt = \left[ \frac{0.2t^{5/2}}{\frac{5}{2}} + 1.4t \right]_4^{16} = \left[ 0.08t^{5/2} + 1.4t \right]_4^{16}$$

Calculate the total distance travelled:
$$s_{\text{total}} = s_1 + s_2 = 7.2 + 96.16 = 103.36\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Because velocity is positive throughout ($v > 0$ for all $t \ge 0$), the particle never reverses direction, so total distance equals total displacement.

Step 1: Distance for the first interval ($0 \le t \le 4$):
Using the given displacement function $s(t) = 0.3t^2 + 0.6t$:
$$s_1 = s(4) - s(0) = [0.3(16) + 0.6(4)] - 0 = 4.8 + 2.4 = 7.2\text{ m}$$

Step 2: Distance for the second interval ($4 \le t \le 16$):
Integrate $v(t) = 0.2t^{3/2} + 1.4$ from $t = 4$ to $t = 16$:
$$s_2 = \int_4^{16} (0.2t^{3/2} + 1.4)\,dt$$
Antiderivative:
$$F(t) = 0.2 \times \frac{t^{5/2}}{\frac{5}{2}} + 1.4t = \frac{0.4}{5}t^{5/2} + 1.4t = 0.08t^{5/2} + 1.4t$$

ai_rubric.Integrating Motion Functions: Evaluates distance in first stage as $7.2\text{ m}$, integrates post-4 velocity to get $F(t) = 0.08t^{5/2} + 1.4t$, evaluates $F(16) - F(4) = 96.16\text{ m}$, and sums to obtain $103.36\text{ m}$.
